reader.requirement: At --std 85 a LINAGE clause whose LINES AT TOP integer-3 or LINES AT BOTTOM integer-4 is zero must be accepted (an exception to the III.2 rule that an integer is neither signed nor zero), and a zero margin, written as a literal or held in data-name-3/4, must add no margin lines to the logical page; integer-1 and integer-2 keep the nonzero default.

edition-consulted.switches: Classify(operand, DialectLevel) calls IntegerSlot.At(dialectLevel); the TOP and BOTTOM slots are IntegerSlot.Zero with Since 0, so zero is permitted at every edition
ZeroMessage cites §1985:III.2 below 2002 and §2023:5.5 1) from 2002 when integer-1 or integer-2 is zero (message text only)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition in IntegerOperandPass.cs, LinageClauseRules.cs, FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs#BindLinageClause and SequentialConnector.cs linage members; the runtime page logic reads no edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1_linage_zero_margins covers literal zeros with no page overflow; not exercised are data-name-3/4 holding zero, a page overflow with zero margins, and the refusal of zero integer-1/integer-2

probes.printed: PZ (LINAGE 2 FOOTING 2 TOP 0 BOTTOM 0) and PD (TOP WT BOTTOM WB, both 0) step LC 2,1,2,1,2 identically over page overflow; bytes of both files: one CRLF then each record on its own line, no margin lines; PT (TOP 1 BOTTOM 1) carries extra blank lines per page
probes.expected: GR1: logical page = body + 0 + 0; GR4/GR5 the value may be zero, so a zero margin adds no lines and a literal zero equals a data-name holding zero

probes.printed: COBOL2386 LINAGE IS 0 LINES and COBOL2386 WITH FOOTING AT 0, each citing §1985:III.2
probes.expected: §1985:III.2: integer is neither signed nor zero unless the format's rules allow it; SR4 allows only integer-3 and integer-4

probes.printed: data-name operands PIC 9 VALUE 0 accepted and behave as the literal zero
probes.expected: GR4/GR5: the value may be zero

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.7.3 SR4  (║3.7.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR4
OK  §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR4  (║3.7.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: The one integer-operand screen classifies TOP and BOTTOM as zero-permitted at every edition and refuses zero for integer-1 and integer-2 with the 1985 citation. At run time a zero margin, literal or data-name, writes no margin lines while a margin of 1 does, so the zero is handled as a value, not dropped.

refuter.evidence: l1.cob (runs/l1-001, exit 0): FD PZ LINAGE 3 TOP 000 BOTTOM 00, PT TOP 2 BOTTOM 1, PD TOP WT BOTTOM WB with WT 0 at OPEN, 2 before WRITE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE, 0 before WRITE BEFORE ADVANCING PAGE. od -c of the files: PZ newlines before A1/A2/A4 = 1/2/4, PT = 3/5/7 (exactly +top, +bottom+top), PD = 1/4/4, i.e. the zero margin adds no lines, the data-name margin changed to 2 at ADVANCING PAGE adds 2 lines to the next page only and back to 0 adds none (GR7b). l2.cob: TOP +0 and BOTTOM -0 refused COBOL0001/COBOL1970 (integer is unsigned). l3.cob: TOP ZERO refused COBOL5506 (figurative is not an integer), BOTTOM 0.0 refused COBOL5506. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.7.3 SR4 'Integer-3, integer-4 may be zero'; OK §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR5 'specifies the number of lines that comprise the bottom margin'; OK §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR7 'at the time a WRITE statement with the ADVANCING PAGE phrase is executed'.
